summary: myidsan gains a self-service TOTP second factor (RFC 6238, pure-Go infra/mfa package + a new github.com/skip2/go-qrcode dependency for on-box QR rendering -- no CDN, air-gap safe) for the credentials it verifies itself: local password and LDAP/AD. A self-service Profile page (opened from the account chip) lets any signed-in user enroll (scan a QR or enter the base32 secret manually), confirm, view status, regenerate 10 single-use bcrypt-hashed recovery codes, and disable their own factor (GET/POST/DELETE /api/mfa/*). Once a factor is confirmed, both password login surfaces -- the SPA's POST /api/login/default and /api/login/ldap, and the server-rendered /api/auth/login page -- withhold the session cookie after a correct password and instead return an opaque, single-use, 5-minute, client-fingerprint-bound challenge token; the session is only issued after the token plus a TOTP or recovery code is redeemed at POST /api/login/mfa (SPA) or POST /api/auth/mfa (server-rendered). Kerberos SPNEGO and OIDC/Google/GitHub logins are deliberately not gated -- the upstream IdP owns factor policy for those. The shared secret is sealed at rest the same way the LDAP bind password already is. A superadmin can clear another user's factor at DELETE /api/mfa-admin/{id}; a new RESET_MFA marker file in the data dir (mirroring the existing RESET_ADMIN password-recovery marker) clears the stock superadmin's own factor on next boot for the sole-superadmin lost-device lockout case. A new myidsan_mfa_challenge_total{result} metric tracks issued/success/failed/expired outcomes so a spike in failures flags online guessing against a known password. Separately, myidsan is now listed as an available, downloadable product on the r450k marketing/download site (tag namespace myidsan-v, image ghcr.io/mysayasan/myidsan), joining mymatasan/myiotsan/myseliasan -- its release pipeline already existed but was not yet surfaced to visitors.
compatibility: Purely additive and opt-in: two new DB tables (user_mfa_factor, user_mfa_recovery_code, auto-added by bootstrap schema generation), no changes to any existing table, endpoint, or config default. An existing install upgrades with MFA fully disabled for every account until that account's owner explicitly enrolls -- local and LDAP logins behave exactly as before for any account with no confirmed factor. There is no mfa.policy/required-role setting; enrollment is self-serve only in this release (a future required-for-some-roles policy remains a valid follow-up, see docs/MYIDSAN_MFA_PLAN.md). The RESET_MFA marker requires local filesystem access to the data dir, matching RESET_ADMIN's threat model, and clears only the second factor, never the password.
